issues.where: signals(): '# (c) a leftover long from an earlier week ... s.exit_long[sig] = True'
issues.issue: Rule (c), the leftover-position guard, is an addition that is not in the pre-registered rules. I checked it against executor._execute. The manage step reads exit_long[i - 1] only for i > e_i. When the strategy is flat at sig, the new trade fills at the open of ei (e_i = ei), and its first exit check reads exit_long[ei], never exit_long[sig], so the marker cannot touch the new trade. When an old position is still open at sig, it closes at the open of ei and this week's entry is lost. The executor would have blocked that entry anyway, because the signal at sig is not registered while a position is open. Without (c), the stale trade would run to this week's Friday exit. On the design years, entries equal trades in all 8 cells I ran (USATECHIDXUSD and JPNIDXJPY, season and ctrl, n_weeks 4 and 5), so no week was lost.
issues.fix: No code change. The Director should record (c), and the change from the d+7 Monday 12:00 end to the next entered week's entry time in (b), as documented deviations that serve the rule's stated purpose.

issues.where: signals(): fallback block '(b) causal fallback ... s.exit_long[a:b] = True'
issues.issue: The fallback works as intended, but the 2013 data gaps produce multi-day holds that are not a Monday-to-Friday exposure. Examples: USATECHIDXUSD season n_weeks 5, entry 2013-05-13, exit 2013-05-22 16:00 across a 120 h gap with no bars; JPNIDXJPY ctrl, entry 2013-09-23, exit 2013-10-02 01:00 across a 105 h gap; USATECHIDXUSD ctrl, entry 2013-04-08, exit 2013-04-15 15:00 across a 71 h gap. Each exits one bar after the first post-gap bar, which is the specified engine semantics: a marker on bar j closes at the open of j+1. The longest hold is 9.0 days. Any stop crossed during a gap is filled at the post-gap open.
issues.fix: No code change. In reporting, count these as fallback exits, as already required, and show the season-minus-ctrl difference D with and without 2013. The charter says index data is patchy before 2014.

lookahead_risk: Low. Week selection is calendar-only: q0, off and s0 come from the Monday date and the symbol. ATR20 comes from F.atr_prev, which is shifted to be known at the start of the trading day, and is read at ei. The 90-minute delay limit means ei always falls in Monday's trading day, so sig is either in that same day or the last bar of an earlier, completed day, and ATR20[ei] is known at sig's close. The skip on m.ts[ei] is the same execution-feasibility check the oracle strategies use ('the market opened by 16:00'). Whether a week counts as entered, and so where the previous fallback window ends, depends only on ts[ei'] and ATR[ei'] of the next week. That decision changes markers only on bars at or after ei', so it is causal. The fallback start (Friday 20:00) and end (the next entered week's Monday 14:30) are timestamps located by searchsorted on m.ts. They never use bar counts, and every marked bar is at or before sig_next, which is before the next fill at ei_next. The automated checker reports truncation (2 probes), perturbation (4 probes) and determinism all clean with 217 entries. The module on disk is byte-identical to the reviewed text once CRLF line endings are removed.
notes: Second review, after the blocker fix. My earlier blocker is resolved. The fallback window now runs from Friday 20:00 of each entered week to the entry time of the next entered week, or to the end of the data for the last one. A season position can no longer run into control weeks, and the reverse also holds. I verified the rest against the rules. q0 and off match the unit checks (month index % 12 % 3). s0 adds jp_shift_days only for symbols starting with 'JPN'. season = s0 <= off < s0 + 7*n_weeks, and ctrl is its complement. Any other arm raises ValueError. Entry is a long market order at sig = ei - 1, with entry_type 0, valid_bars 1, sl_dist = sl_atr * ATR20[ei] (always > 0 because non-finite and <= 0 values are skipped), tp NaN by default and max_bars 0. The normal exit sets exit_long[xi - 1] when xi > ei and ts[xi] is no more than 180 min after Friday 19:30. No week is skipped because of Friday bars. Every grid key (arm, start_off, n_weeks, sl_atr) and every fixed key is read from p, and PARAMS holds all of them. Structural run on design data only (end 2018-01-01; I did not look at R statistics). USATECHIDXUSD: season 77 (n_weeks 4) and 97 (n_weeks 5) entries, ctrl 174 and 154. That fits the pre-registered 70-90 for season; ctrl at 174 is slightly above the expected 140-170 but plausible for 2013-2017. JPNIDXJPY: season 70 and 88, ctrl 160 and 142. Every entry fills at Monday 15:00 UTC. All signal exits are at Friday 20:00 except the gap cases listed under issues, plus 2 Sunday-evening fallback exits in each ctrl cell. For the Director: at sl_atr 1.0 about half the season trades are stopped out before Friday (41 of 77 on USATECHIDXUSD, n_weeks 4). That follows from the pre-registered stop width, not from a code defect, but it means the sl_atr 1.0 cells measure a stop-truncated drift. Weigh the 1.0 and 2.0 cells as a family rather than picking the better one.
